title: Example and Instance (2025)
headline: Algorithm 1 does not always meet its stated approximation guarantee. The authors agreed.

work.title: Greedy Scheduling with Machine Preferences
work.venue: Proceedings of the Conference on Algorithmic Choice (ACAC 2025)

claims.label: Algorithm 1 (steps 3 and 4)
claims.gist: Greedy assignment is within a factor of two of the optimal makespan.
claims.statement: For identical jobs and machines with preferences, Algorithm 1 returns a schedule whose makespan is at most twice the optimum.

result.summary: A three-machine instance where the makespan is three times the optimum.
result.witness: Step 3 can assign every job to the machine that ranks it highest even when that machine is already full, and step 4 never rebalances. The instance and the trace are in the evidence package.
result.tested: All instances with three machines and up to nine jobs.
not_claimed: A factor-two schedule is not claimed to be impossible.

vor_check.detail: Statement, definitions and the decisive step checked on rendered pages of the published version.

checks.detail: The researcher traced the algorithm by hand on the instance.
The authors agreed that step 3 needs a capacity check.

reproduction.detail: The evidence package reruns with one command (Python 3.12, standard library only).

claims.novelty: No earlier report found in the searched literature.

author_position.summary: The authors agreed and plan to post a revised version with a capacity check in step 3.

statements.ai_use: Discovery and the separate rechecks used AI models in separate sessions. The independent reproduction, the version-of-record check and every editorial decision were done by the researcher.
